# aether_cluster (Resource)

A managed Kubernetes cluster (control plane). Node pools are separate `aether_node_pool` resources. Creation waits until the cluster is `running` (or `degraded`, reported as a warning); a `k8s_version` change performs an in-place upgrade through the upgrade endpoint and must move forward.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "aether_k8s_versions" "offered" {}

resource "aether_cluster" "prod" {
  name   = "prod"
  region = "eu-fi"
  # latest is null while the platform's version window is unavailable; pin a
  # minor instead (e.g. "1.37") if that's not acceptable.
  k8s_version = data.aether_k8s_versions.offered.latest
  # Defaults to true: the public API endpoint is billed as one public IP (€4/month).
  public_endpoint = true
}

# Fixed pool: a flat monthly fee for desired_nodes nodes.
resource "aether_node_pool" "workers" {
  cluster_id    = aether_cluster.prod.id
  name          = "workers"
  vcpus         = 4
  memory_gb     = 16
  disk_gb       = 80
  desired_nodes = 3
}

# Autoscaling pool: a vCPU/memory budget with max > min makes it autoscaling (billed hourly per node).
resource "aether_node_pool" "burst" {
  cluster_id    = aether_cluster.prod.id
  name          = "burst"
  vcpus         = 4
  memory_gb     = 16
  disk_gb       = 80
  min_vcpus     = 4
  max_vcpus     = 32
  min_memory_gb = 16
  max_memory_gb = 128
}

data "aether_kubeconfig" "prod" {
  cluster_id = aether_cluster.prod.id
}

output "kubeconfig" {
  value     = data.aether_kubeconfig.prod.content
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `k8s_version` (String) `MAJOR.MINOR` (the platform resolves it to the latest offered patch) or an explicit `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` of an offered minor. A bare `1.37` is treated as equal to whichever `1.37.x` the platform resolved it to, so the resolved patch never shows as drift. Changes go through an in-place upgrade, which must move forward and be INCREMENTAL: a higher patch of the same minor, or exactly the next minor. A backwards move is refused at plan; a skipped minor is rejected by the API at apply. After `terraform import`, state holds the resolved `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, so if the configuration says `MAJOR.MINOR` the first plan shows a one-time in-place update of the version spelling; applying it changes nothing in the platform (the provider only re-reads the cluster).
- `name` (String) Cluster name. Changing it renames the cluster in place.
- `region` (String) Region id from `data.aether_regions` (e.g. `eu-fi`). Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Optional

- `plan` (String) Package slug (`dev`, `starter`, `growth`, `scale`); omit to be billed per resource. Must not be empty. Immutable: changing it replaces the cluster.
- `public_endpoint` (Boolean) Expose the API server on a public IPv4 address and DNS name. Defaults to `true` — the public API endpoint, billed as one public IP per month (see the platform's pricing); omitting the attribute therefore creates the endpoint and incurs that charge. `false` is still accepted by the API but is not a supported configuration (vendored OpenAPI, tracked internally as I-14): the cluster has NO supported access path from outside the platform (no laptop or CI access). Immutable: changing it replaces the cluster. Removing it from the configuration plans the default (`true`), which replaces a cluster created with `false` — including an imported cluster that reads `false`; set `public_endpoint = false` explicitly to keep it.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `capi_cluster_name` (String) Internal Cluster API name of the cluster.
- `ceph_pool` (String) Storage pool of the cluster.
- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339).
- `endpoint` (String) API server URL, once the cluster is provisioned far enough to report one.
- `harbor_project` (String) Registry project associated with the cluster.
- `id` (String) Cluster UUID.
- `keycloak_realm` (String) Identity realm of the cluster.
- `lb_subnet` (String) Load-balancer subnet allocated at create time.
- `observed_kubernetes_version` (String) Kubernetes version the control plane reports once a rollout settles.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status reported by the API (`provisioning`, `running`, `upgrading`, `degraded`, `failed`, ...).
- `status_message` (String) Human explanation accompanying the status, when the API offers one.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time (RFC 3339).
- `worker_subnet` (String) Per-cluster worker /24 allocated at create time.

### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
